correctness.rationale: The weight-1 and weight-2 sums of a character of weight j are T_j=(q−1)n−qj and U_j=(T_j²−(q−2)T_j−n(q−1))/2; the remaining nonzero shells sum to −1−T_j−U_j. This remains valid for composite q. The strictly concave multiplier as a function of T_j is maximized at the lattice point nearest (q−2)/2−R(p); the strict inequalities 2<R(p)<3 for 0<p<1 yield the stated unique floor index. At p=0 all nonconstant eigenvalues are −1, and at p=1 a four-coordinate subspace has a weight-3 eigenvalue q−1>0. Strict downward propagation of finite negative type then gives existence, uniqueness and the full threshold range; centering and taking the rank of the Gram matrix proves the embedding claims. The two limits follow by testing p=c/n with fixed q and p=c/q with fixed n, using bounded t in the first case and t=q−n, u=−(n−1)q+n(n−1)/2 in the second. Independent replay: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -B /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 4; it checks 16 real tensor-layer comparisons and four full powered-distance nullities, not the general theorem.
